data_status_warning: All data are AI-extracted and unverified (pre–TASK-014). Treat study characteristics, outcome definitions, time windows, numerators/denominators, and reported effect measures as provisional. Several records appear to overlap (e.g., SCR_000003 and SCR_000024) and some outcomes mix time frames (e.g., AKI at 1 year). Do not pool or reclassify any value without human verification against source PDFs.
executive_recommendation: Narrow the scope. Make the primary meta-analysis the effect of perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors on postoperative acute kidney injury within 7 days, restricted to randomized trials with preoperative or immediate perioperative exposure. Keep observational AKI evidence as a secondary analysis (separate from RCTs). Handle euglycemic ketoacidosis, mortality, MACE, and length of stay by narrative synthesis or highly selective exploratory analyses due to heterogeneous definitions/time windows and sparse/zero-event patterns.
recommended_topic: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors to prevent 7-day postoperative AKI after adult cardiac surgery
recommended_title: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors and 7-day postoperative acute kidney injury after adult cardiac surgery: randomized evidence with observational corroboration
recommended_primary_question: Among adults undergoing open cardiac surgery, does starting an SGLT2 inhibitor preoperatively or in the immediate perioperative period (before or around the day of surgery and continued through early postoperative days) reduce the risk of acute kidney injury within 7 postoperative days compared with no SGLT2 inhibitor/placebo?

recommended_pico.population: Adults undergoing open cardiac surgical procedures (CABG, valve, combined; predominantly with cardiopulmonary bypass)
recommended_pico.intervention_or_exposure: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor therapy initiated preoperatively (typically 1–3 days before surgery or chronically before surgery with perioperative hold) and/or continued through postoperative day 2–5
recommended_pico.comparator: Placebo or standard care without SGLT2 inhibitor
recommended_pico.outcome: Acute kidney injury stage ≥1 by KDIGO (or equivalent AKIN stage ≥1 / RIFLE ‘Risk’ or worse)
recommended_pico.study_design: Primary: randomized controlled trials. Secondary: adjusted observational cohorts analyzed separately.

recommended_primary_endpoint: Postoperative acute kidney injury within 7 days (KDIGO stage ≥1 or AKIN stage ≥1 or RIFLE ‘Risk’ or worse; creatinine-based preferred, urine-output accepted if per guideline definition)
recommended_secondary_endpoints: In-hospital or 30-day all-cause mortality (descriptive; not pooled across heterogeneous designs)
Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis within 72 hours post-op using biochemical criteria and prespecified sampling (narrative; pooling not advised with current dataset)
Major adverse cardiovascular events at 30 days (RCTs only, if consistently defined; otherwise narrative)
Length of hospital stay (narrative due to medians-only reporting and inconsistent definitions)

candidate_topics.topic: Perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors and 7-day postoperative AKI (randomized trials)
candidate_topics.clinical_question: Do perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors reduce KDIGO-defined AKI within 7 days after adult cardiac surgery versus placebo/standard care?
candidate_topics.primary_endpoint: AKI within 7 postoperative days (KDIGO stage ≥1 or equivalent)
candidate_topics.rationale: Clinically central, mechanistically plausible, and most consistently reported. Four RCTs report this endpoint or near-equivalent windows; definitions largely KDIGO-aligned; effect data are available or reported as RR.
candidate_topics.clinical_coherence: High (perioperative timing; similar surgical contexts; AKI captured within 5–7 days)
candidate_topics.methodological_coherence: High (restricted to RCTs; separable from observational evidence; compatible effect measures)
candidate_topics.publication_value: High—recent large multicenter RCT plus supportive smaller RCTs; substantial readership interest and practice relevance
major_limitations: One RCT provides RR without raw counts (SCR_000098)
Exposure regimens vary (chronic preop with periop hold vs 1–3-day periop dosing)
One RCT used composite KDIGO/AKIN/RIFLE definition

candidate_topics.topic: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure and 7-day postoperative AKI (observational cohorts)
candidate_topics.clinical_question: Among adults undergoing cardiac surgery, is preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure associated with reduced KDIGO-defined AKI within 7 days versus nonuse?
candidate_topics.rationale: Multiple adjusted cohorts with compatible early AKI windows; valuable as sensitivity/triangulation separate from RCTs.
candidate_topics.clinical_coherence: Moderate (urgent/emergent vs elective; exposure windows differ)
candidate_topics.methodological_coherence: Moderate (adjusted RR vs adjusted OR; entropy weighting vs PSM; mix of 48 h vs 7 d windows)
candidate_topics.publication_value: Moderate—useful corroboration but confounding remains; best framed as secondary evidence
major_limitations: Effect measures not uniform (RR vs OR)
Time windows vary (48 h vs 7 d)
Residual confounding likely despite causal methods

candidate_topics.topic: Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (eDKA) in the immediate postoperative period
candidate_topics.clinical_question: Does perioperative SGLT2 inhibitor exposure increase the risk of biochemically confirmed euglycemic ketoacidosis in the first 24–72 hours after cardiac surgery?
candidate_topics.primary_endpoint: Biochemically confirmed postoperative ketoacidosis within 24–72 hours (acidosis + ketones; specify euglycemia threshold)
candidate_topics.rationale: Clinically important safety concern; conflicting signals (zero events in several RCTs vs high incidence when systematically sampled in one cohort).
candidate_topics.clinical_coherence: Low—definitions and ascertainment strategies vary widely; some rely on symptomatic testing only
candidate_topics.methodological_coherence: Low—zero-event pairs common; heavy detection bias; different biochemical thresholds and sampling schedules
candidate_topics.publication_value: Moderate (safety signal worth discussing), but meta-analysis currently unjustified
major_limitations: Potential duplication of perioperative policies (drug holds) not harmonized

candidate_topics.topic: Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after cardiac surgery
candidate_topics.clinical_question: Do perioperative SGLT2 inhibitors reduce MACE after cardiac surgery?
candidate_topics.primary_endpoint: MACE at a uniform timepoint (preferably 30 days, RCTs only)
candidate_topics.rationale: Important but sparse and heterogeneous (30 days vs 1 year vs 5 years; varying definitions)
candidate_topics.methodological_coherence: Low—mix of RCT vs long-term observational designs; composite definitions differ
major_limitations: Insufficient trials reporting a common window

outcome_harmonization.recommended_harmonized_endpoint: AKI within 7 postoperative days, defined as KDIGO stage ≥1 (increase in serum creatinine ≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h or ≥1.5× baseline within 7 days, or urine output <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h). If a study used AKIN stage ≥1 or RIFLE ‘Risk’ or worse, treat as compatible.
outcome_harmonization.recommended_time_window: Postoperative day 0 through day 7 (inclusive). If only 120 h is available, treat as within the 7-day window.
compatible_definitions: KDIGO stage ≥1 using creatinine and/or urine output
AKIN stage ≥1 using creatinine and/or urine output
definitions_or_timepoints_to_separate: AKI assessed only within 48 hours (analyze separately if heterogeneity is high)
AKI beyond the early postoperative period (e.g., 30 days, 1 year)
AKI severity subgrades (stage 2–3) if analyzed as separate endpoints
outcome_harmonization.preferred_effect_measure: Risk ratio (log scale). Use reported RR where provided; otherwise derive from 2×2 counts for trials.
outcome_harmonization.recommendation: Use this for the primary RCT meta-analysis. Keep 48-hour-only and long-term AKI separate.

outcome_harmonization.recommended_harmonized_endpoint: Biochemically confirmed euglycemic ketoacidosis within 72 hours post-op, requiring metabolic acidosis (pH <7.30 or HCO3− <18 mmol/L) plus ketonemia/ketonuria (prefer β‑hydroxybutyrate ≥3.0 mmol/L), with glucose <200 mg/dL.
outcome_harmonization.recommended_time_window: 0–72 hours after surgery (ICU admission to POD3).
compatible_definitions: Strict eDKA definitions with prespecified sampling times and full acid-base/ketone panels
definitions_or_timepoints_to_separate: Broad ‘ketoacidosis’ definitions using low ketone cutoffs (e.g., ≥0.6 mmol/L)
Event capture limited to symptom-triggered testing
In-hospital or 30-day windows without standardized sampling
outcome_harmonization.preferred_effect_measure: Risk ratio if nonzero events and comparable denominators; otherwise narrative comparison.
outcome_harmonization.recommendation: Do not pool with current dataset; present narrative synthesis and highlight detection-bias sensitivity.

heterogeneity_drivers: Exposure timing and duration (chronic preop with periop hold vs 1–3-day periop dosing vs postoperative initiation)
Surgery type and technique (on-pump vs off-pump; CABG vs valve vs aortic; elective vs urgent/emergent)
AKI definition and assessment window (48 h vs 120 h vs 7 days vs 1 year)
Use of urine-output criteria vs creatinine-only
Study design (blinded RCT vs open-label RCT vs PSM/weighted observational)
Effect measure and adjustment (RR vs OR; crude vs adjusted; matching vs weighting)
Baseline renal function and comorbidity profiles (CKD, diabetes prevalence, LVEF)
Perioperative SGLT2i management (withhold timing, resume timing)
outcomes_better_for_narrative_synthesis: Euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis (due to disparate definitions and ascertainment)
In-hospital or 30-day mortality (sparse events; mixed windows/designs)
Major adverse cardiovascular events (heterogeneous definitions and timepoints)
Length of hospital/ICU stay (medians only; inconsistent definitions)
protocol_and_reporting_cautions: Avoid double counting between SCR_000003 and SCR_000024 (appear to report the same 55-patient pilot). Use SCR_000024 for AKI counts.
Do not mix AKI at 1 year (SCR_000059) with early postoperative AKI (≤7 days).
Keep RCT and observational evidence strictly separate in analyses and conclusions.
For SCR_000098, only RR is reported; confirm denominators if attempting to derive counts.
Harmonize AKI to KDIGO stage ≥1 within 7 days; treat 48-hour-only reports (SCR_000113) as a separate exploratory set.
eDKA definitions vary widely; only pool if strict biochemical criteria and prespecified sampling windows match across studies.
Check that POST-CABGDM (SCR_000012) withheld the SGLT2i 72 h pre-op; note this exposure nuance in interpretation.
Confirm whether urine-output criteria were used; if mixed, prioritize creatinine-based KDIGO for harmonization.
Ensure one effect per study per meta-analysis (no multiple cohorts/definitions from the same trial).
